- **Damaged photos come back from an upload (FL-1472):** uploading or importing a good copy of a damaged photo now puts it in the damaged file's place, from the web, the desktop app, your phones, Google Takeout or Eagle, instead of being turned away as a duplicate. The damaged file is kept beside it, and Undo puts it back.
- **The true original replaces a repair (FL-1472):** when Library care repaired a damaged photo and its original turns up later, the original takes the repair's place instead of arriving as a second photo.
- **Every importer puts photos back (FL-1472):** web downloads, browser captures and Preservation restores now bring back a missing or damaged photo they find again, and Takeout and Eagle no longer count it as a new photo or overwrite its details.
- **iCloud Photos helps fix problem files (FL-1472):** when a missing or damaged photo came from iCloud Photos, Library care asks iCloud for it right away and gets it first. iCloud items that failed or were waiting for review are tried again while their photo needs it, and the file's history says when iCloud had the original.
- **Fixed files stay fixed in the list (FL-1472):** a fixed file keeps how and when it was fixed, so Fixed for you stays accurate and clears after 30 days.
- **The last good copy is never emptied (FL-1473):** Unused files keeps a copy while a photo with the same file is missing or damaged, so emptying it can't delete the only good copy.
- **Clutter can be suggested for the Archive (FL-1469):** memes, receipts, screenshots, shop photos, forwarded chat images, whiteboards, notes to self and accidental shots can be suggested for the Archive. Nothing is deleted, and nothing moves unless you choose it.
